This study evaluates the effectiveness of three approaches to training classifiers when the training data contains noisy labels: NCA, a basic thresholding approach, NCA-N, an adjusted version that draws samples from the training batch before sorting; and NCA-L, which learns a logistic noise model from the training data. The performance of NCA was previously established in a specific regime of label noise, but this study explores its performance in a more general setting. The results show that NCA outperforms its own baseline, but can be outclassed by NCA-N and NCA-L in certain cases. The NCA-L approach demonstrates strong performance across most scenarios, but its ability to learn the noise model is hindered by the presence of large label noise, but not by noise levels typical of NCA's established domain.

In the case of a fixed even subset S of the 24-element set Gamma, consisting of the 12 antipodal pairs of elements in Gamma along with 6 additional elements, a code is formed by the orbits of the subgroup of order 4 produced by the group Gamma with S as a defining set. We identify the automorphism groups, determine the number of orbits under different automorphism groups, and classify the possible symmetries for the resulting code when S is a proper non-empty subset of Gamma, with specific considerations given for the possible configurations when S is empty or entire Gamma.

A binary system within the M67 open cluster has been identified, featuring a near 0.5-day orbital period and near zero-eclipse light curve. By combining radial velocity data from high-resolution spectra and precise photometric observations from K2 satellite, the binary's orbital elements were accurately determined. Utilizing Gaia's and K2's information, the companion star's mass and specific gravity were calculated. By cross-referencing the binary system with the M67 cluster's main sequence, the binary's orbital period was matched to a turnoff star candidate. By combining the binary's orbital elements with isochrone data, the binary's orbital parameters and the age of the M67 cluster were determined, yielding an age of approximately 3.2 billion years and consistent with previous findings.

The given complex Schrödinger operator $\mathscr L_c$ combines elements of the harmonic oscillator operator and the complex Liouville operator. We prove that the set of non-trivial eigenfunctions associated with $\mathscr L_c$ form a complete system of functions on $\mathbb C$. To establish this, we first determine the eigenvalues and show that these eigenvalues are bounded, leading to the conclusion that the set of eigenfunctions forms an orthonormal set on $\mathbb C$. We then demonstrate that these eigenfunctions are linearly independent and, as a result, the collection forms a complete set of functions on $\mathbb C$. As an application of this result, we show that any non-trivial function $f$ in $\mathbb C$ can be represented as a linear combination of the eigenfunctions associated with $\mathscr L_c$. We also derive a formula for the minimal number of terms required for this representation.

A revised density-based variable neigbourhood search algorithm for SPH has been developed to enhance its accuracy, particularly in conserving momentum and capturing the physical properties of water. The modified model incorporates a refined method for evaluating the volume of particles and improved neighbor selection, resulting in increased computational efficiency. The addition of a cohesive force within the algorithm enables the representation of solid and liquid states in the system. The performance of the new model was evaluated by analyzing the simulation of a spherical drop of water, water drop impact, and the collision of two identical water bodies. The results demonstrated that the revised model successfully conserves both momentum and energy and produces more realistic representations of water flow.

Recent advancements in hyperspectral imaging have been hindered by the high costs associated with acquiring, processing, and storing these images. To overcome this limitation, researchers have focused on developing methods to reconstruct hyperspectral images from lower-cost, RGB images by reducing the number of spectral bands captured. Building on existing work in spectral super-resolution, this research proposes a novel network architecture that leverages multi-scale, multi-resolution, and multi-scale pixel-aware features to enhance spectral super-resolution performance. The network incorporates a pixel-aware module to capture detailed, local image information and a function-blend module to model the non-linear relationships between different spectral bands. By combining these features, the network is able to effectively capture the complex, non-linear relationships between RGB and hyperspectral images. Experimental results on synthetic and real datasets demonstrate the network's ability to achieve high-quality spectral super-resolution results, with significant improvements in PSNR and spectral information preservation compared to state-of-the-art methods.

Item geotagging is a form of weakly supervised learning that has gained significant attention, but current approaches often rely on a single global positioning system, neglecting the local context of the item. Our research demonstrates that incorporating local features in conjunction with the global positioning system improves geotagging performance. To achieve this, we developed a novel network architecture that generates a local descriptor for each item and trains a geotagger to predict these contexts. Experimental results on real-world datasets show that our proposed method outperforms traditional models based on a single global positioning system, and the availability of high-quality local positioning information significantly enhances geotagging performance.

The issue of unverified dam reservoirs worldwide is a pressing concern that needs attention. Once a dam is constructed, its environmental and social effects can be irreversible. To prevent these issues, it is essential to identify and locate dams before they are built. However, a significant number of dams have been constructed without being officially registered, which is why monitoring from a distance using satellite imagery can be a valuable tool in finding these hidden structures. A recent study developed a novel approach that uses deep learning algorithms to find dam reservoirs in this manner. By training a neural network to recognize the patterns of dam reservoirs in a dataset of satellite images, it is possible to locate potential dam reservoirs anywhere in the world. Furthermore, it is possible to use this method to retrieve information about the dam reservoirs themselves, which is why the researchers also developed a loss function that encourages the network to produce accurate results. Using this approach, it is possible to retrieve information about the dam reservoirs and their location.

This research introduces a novel quantum concept called Quantum Financial System region, defined as QFS-region, leveraging the principles of quantum finance and quantum mechanics. The paper outlines the underlying mathematical framework, utilizing the tensor product space of classical financial instruments, and derives a fundamental relationship governing quantum financial states. These relationships provide a theoretical framework for analyzing and manipulating QFS-region in quantum financial space, with far-reaching implications for quantum financial markets.

The task of predicting the type of attraction, such as monument, museum, or restaurant, given a geotagged tweet with a point-of-interest (POI) tag, is referred to as POIP. This task is significant for various applications, including location-based services and task automation. Despite the importance of POIP, it has been largely understudied. POIP involves a multi-modal input consisting of an image and geotagged text, and it can be viewed as a multi-label multi-media multi-task classification problem. This paper introduces a multi-modal POIP task, and it proposes a multi-modal fusion network called the POIPNet, which is designed to effectively extract features from images and text, and to learn multi-task relationships. POIPNet is composed of a convolutional neural network-based image feature extractor, a pre-trained BERT-based text feature extractor, and a multi-layer perceptron (MLP) for multi-task classification. Experimental results show that POIPNet achieves a high POIP accuracy of 0.822, and it significantly outperforms existing methods.

The motivations behind investors' reactions to positive or negative corporate news, as revealed by stock market trends, are complex and multifaceted. This study examines how stock prices respond to positive or negative mentions in corporate earnings calls by analyzing the stock prices of companies that released calls between 2014 and 2017. Specifically, the research focuses on how stock prices move after transcripts related to earnings calls are publicly released, taking into account various factors, including the tone and topic of discussion. To identify the tone of calls, the researchers employed a model that combines the Conference of the Konvectors and BERT language models. Additionally, the study explores the significance of conversation topics and tone using a model that quantifies their impact on stock price movements.

This research focuses on the problem of placing sensors in a network to cover a specific area, taking into account varying communication ranges and different types of sensors. The goal is to find the most effective sensor placement using a novel approach that combines genetic algorithms and Voronoi partitioning, aiming to minimize costs and ensure complete coverage in both homogeneous and heterogeneous network configurations. The proposed method is demonstrated to outperform traditional grid-based placement under different scenarios, as evidenced by the experimental results.

We introduce a quantum state filtering approach that utilizes polynomials to identify low-weight vectors within quantum states. This method is then integrated with the quantum approximate minimization oracle technique to solve linear systems more efficiently. The integration yields optimal hybrid algorithms that minimize query complexity while requiring fewer than logarithmic levels of entanglement. Notably, we have developed a quantum state filtering method that achieves the best possible query complexity of O(ε^(-1) and and achieves this with a very low level of entanglement.

We investigate the characteristics of compact gauged infant skyrmions within a nonlinear dielectric environment, using a non-linear theory of gauge fields. By incorporating a gauge field into the standard Skyrme model, our non-linear theory captures the dynamics of topological defects that occur during phase transitions in the early universe. In particular, our research focuses on infant skyrmions that form in the expanding universe during the early stages of matter formation, and we examine their behavior within a non-linear medium. Through numerical simulations, we reveal the properties of stable compact gauged infant skyrmions, and show that their size and internal structure are significantly influenced by the non-linear environment. Furthermore, our results indicate that the size of these skyrmions is directly related to the non-linearity parameter of the medium, and that it decreases as this parameter increases.

This thesis examines the Standard Model through the lens of the Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT), a theoretical framework that expands upon the Standard Model by introducing new, high-energy scale particles through higher-dimensional operators. This work delves into the implications of these new particles on the behavior of various Standard Model particles, focusing on the strong sector and the Higgs sector. It also investigates the potential of future experiments at lepton and hadron colliders to discover signs of these new particles, even if they are not directly observable.

A nuclear spin gyroscope has been developed to measure the angular deviation of a rotating diamond with a nitrogen-vacancy center ensemble. The device functions by applying a magnetic field that causes the diamond's nuclear spins to precess in sync with its rotation, then measuring the resulting change in spin resonance frequency. By utilizing this data, the device can accurately determine the angular deviation of the diamond as it rotates. The gyroscope's performance is demonstrated by showing its operation in various environments, including space, naval applications, and turbulence measurement, highlighting its potential for use in a wide range of applications.

Cellular behavior is determined by the intricate dance of molecular interactions, necessitating the use of complex models to capture the entire cell's dynamics. The development of such models has significant implications, as they can serve as a bridge between experimental data, cellular processes, and engineered cellular responses. This review aims to provide a unified framework for the field of complete-cell technology by identifying key aspects, such as design considerations, data requirements, and the integration of advanced methods, to facilitate a multidisciplinary approach and guide researchers in creating accurate models that drive precise cellular manipulation.

We introduce Mobile Multi-View Object Picture Search, an innovative mobile picture search system that retrieves similar images of the same object based on a query image, taking into account the object's pose. This system is unique in that it can identify an object's pose within a picture, allowing it to provide the most relevant similar images. Our research involves a novel mobile app that utilizes a mobile device's camera to capture a picture, then searches and retrieves similar images of the object within the same picture. To accomplish this, we have developed a novel technique called Object Pose-Guided Retrieval, which utilizes a pose estimator to identify the object's pose and a pose-invariant image descriptor to retrieve similar images of the object within the same pose. This technique enables the creation of a database that stores pose-invariant image descriptors and object pose information, allowing the system to retrieve similar images of the object within the same pose. Our research has shown that the proposed system significantly outperforms traditional picture search systems that do not consider the object's pose.

Epilepsy affects 1 in 26 adults, primarily characterized by recurring seizures that can be treated with medication but often require surgical intervention. Continuous monitoring can help identify the optimal treatment approach. Although devices such as EEG can detect seizures, they lack the ability to provide a diagnosis or suggest treatment paths on their own. A novel approach using Hyperdimensional Computing has been proposed to improve seizure detection by incorporating prior knowledge, which can aid in diagnosis and surgical planning. In this study, we investigated the application of HDC in EEG-based seizure detection, comparing various learning strategies and data representations. Our results demonstrate that HDC can learn from a small dataset and achieve performance comparable to HDC using large datasets, while reducing training time.

The Hubble tension, a discrepancy between the local Hubble constant and Planck value, has sparked interest in alternative methods for determining the Hubble constant. Gravitational wave standard siren sources are expected to provide precise measurements of the Hubble constant, with current binary black hole observations yielding a $1\sigma$ uncertainty of $4.4\%$. However, the LISA gravitational wave frequency range may outperform current measurements due to its improved distance and redshift precision. We examine the potential for future LISA observations to constrain the Hubble constant, finding that a binary black hole population of $10^5$ systems detected with $10\%$ measurement error could yield a $1\%$ uncertainty in the Hubble constant, surpassing current precision. Nevertheless, the LISA binary neutron star population is unlikely to significantly improve Hubble constant precision due to its smaller distance and redshift error. We also discuss the potential for future gravitational wave observations to resolve the Hubble tension and outline the necessary steps for achieving this goal.

We introduce QALD-9-plus, an expanded multilingual dataset for question-answering that includes translations of the QALD-9 question dataset into 19 languages, made possible by collaborative efforts of native speakers and linguistic experts. These translations were assessed through a comprehensive evaluation process, combining both automatic metrics and human evaluations to ensure the quality of the dataset. Building upon this improvement, we also developed QALD-9-plus-plus, an extension that adds 100 new questions for each language, increasing the diversity and scope of the questions within the dataset. These enhanced datasets are expected to support and advance the development of natural language question-answering systems for Linked Data, serving as a valuable resource for researchers in the field.

The human brain's ability to think, plan, and adapt is attributed to the brain's executive functions, which are responsible for high-level reasoning and problem-solving. These functions, including reasoning, reasoning-by-example, and reasoning-by-relations, are essential for tasks such as decision-making, perception, and learning. Building on this concept, we propose a new framework, Executive Function, which enables self-learning, perception correction, and efficient information retrieval from data. By incorporating a VAE and a VQ-VAE, our framework can re-sample and re-label perception information, effectively "editing" the original data. To achieve this, we utilize a new technique called hindsight summarization, which compresses data into a concise summary. This approach allows our framework to learn from data without the need for extensive training data, effectively "editing" the information to produce more accurate results. By doing so, we can improve the accuracy of downstream tasks, such as classification and data compression.

Deep learning models have shown remarkable performance in medical image tasks, yet concerns about dataset bias persist. This study investigates the underlying bias within a specific dataset, employing a novel approach to model-free bias identification for both spatial and demographic bias. By quantifying the inherent bias, researchers can develop strategies to mitigate its impact on model training and prediction processes. To gauge image bias, the study utilizes the CINA35 database, which measures the resilience of deep learning models to various bias scenarios. These experiments provide valuable insights for training and predicting models on biased datasets.

This paper addresses the issue of noisy labels in metric learning, caused by inaccurate label assignments, by proposing a new method called Smooth Proxy-Anchor Cost, or SPAAC. SPAAC incorporates a smooth transition between confident and noisy labels to enhance the loss function of metric learning, which comprises two components: a proxy-anchor cost that measures similarity between positive pairs and a proxy-sample cost that measures similarity between samples and their respective anchors. Through experimental results, the proposed SPAAC method has been shown to outperform existing methods in the fields of computer vision and information retrieval when dealing with noisy label issues.

Future large-scale galaxy surveys will yield high-resolution maps of galaxy distribution, offering a precise measurement of cosmological parameters. The density gradient weighted correlation function, a two-point statistic that accounts for substructure, is a promising indicator for cosmological studies. In this study, its cosmic dependence is analyzed and potential biases resulting from the complex galaxy distribution are identified. The correlation function's effectiveness is demonstrated through a simulation-based analysis, revealing that it can accurately determine the matter density parameter, $\Omega_m$, with minimal uncertainty and no dependence on other parameters.

A theoretical model of a $^3\mathrm{He A}+^{4}\mathrm{He}$ system is proposed to investigate the emergence of topological superfluidity. By using the large-$N$ approximation and a mean-field approach, the model's Hamiltonian is formulated in a way that preserves the integrable nature of the Hamiltonian flow. The resulting model, $\mathrm{SO}(5)\mathrm{K}$, is a two-component free fermion model with a specific interaction, and its properties are examined using a combination of analytical and numerical methods. The model, $\mathrm{SO}(5)\mathrm{K}$, is found to exhibit a variety of solutions that represent different types of superfluid phases, including a $^4\mathrm{He}$-rich and a $^{3}\mathrm{He}$-rich phase. The model, $\mathrm{SO}(5)\mathrm{K}$, is also shown to be a useful framework for studying the properties of a $^3\mathrm{He}$ superfluid that is topologically non-trivial.

We've developed a type of photodetector called a MAPD (Micro-Pixel Chamber Detector) that's particularly useful for the most sensitive astroparticle experiments. To improve its performance, we've been working on a new version of the MAPD, called a snowstorm MAPD (sMAPD), which uses a specially designed anode structure to enhance its capabilities. By optimizing this structure, we've been able to significantly boost the statistical accuracy of the photodetectors. In this study, we've taken it a step further by introducing an alternative structure for the anode and evaluating its potential benefits in a series of simulations and experiments.

This research explores the properties of a certain type of topological invariant and demonstrates its applicability to non-simply connected situations. The findings have significant implications for algebraic geometry, particularly in the context of non-standard elliptic curves. The study also touches on a fundamental conjecture proposed by Cohen and also pays attention to some local geometric structures.

A comprehensive investigation of Aurivillius compound Bi$_5$FeTi$_3$O$_{15}$ (BFTO) under high-pressure conditions utilizes nuclear forward scattering (NFS) as a non-destructive, element-specific technique. The NFS study reveals that BFTO's magnetic properties remain stable up to 0.8 GPa, while pressures above 1.1 GPa lead to a significant increase in the BFTO lattice, resulting in a reduced magnetic domain size. The analysis suggests that BFTO's magnetic order is preserved at room temperature, and the reduced domain size is attributed to enhanced domain wall energy, caused by increased lattice distance. The observed phenomenon is consistent with the BRTO phase transformation into the BFTO phase under high pressure.

A new statistical method has been developed to compare the financial costs associated with multiple trading platforms. This method, known as Bayesian Trading Expense Analysis (BTEA), utilizes a Markov chain-based approach that integrates a priori knowledge about the trading process. BTEA is applied to real-time market data to determine the relative effectiveness of different trading algorithms offered by Fidelity, Charles Schwab, and Ally Invest platforms.

We have developed a comprehensive model to design optomechanical filters capable of adjusting their operation over a wide range of wavelengths. This theoretical framework draws on our previous experimental findings, as detailed in our accompanying research, "Optomechanical filters with adjustable operation over 30 nm range". In our model, the mechanical resonator's properties, such as its strength of interaction and storage time, are not predetermined, allowing for greater flexibility in design. Instead, the mechanical resonator's dimensions and placement can be optimized to meet specific requirements. This approach offers a novel method for adjusting optomechanical filters without relying on a pre-existing resonance, thereby expanding their applicability in various photonic systems.

Public health officials utilize a structured decision-making process to evaluate interventions, considering the potential benefits against the costs and taking action when the advantages outweigh the burdens. In the context of public health, interventions can be evaluated based on factors such as the likelihood of a positive outcome, the associated risk, and the required sample size for statistical significance. The COVID-19 pandemic has presented an opportunity for technological innovation in public health, with the collection of relevant data playing a pivotal role. The rise of Web usage as a means of data collection has led to the development of techniques for extracting relevant information from Web content, with the potential to inform public health decision-making. This study investigates the feasibility of using Web content to evaluate public health interventions, with a focus on data-driven methods. The authors examine the strengths and limitations of these approaches and discuss their practical applications in decision-making processes.

A novel neural-based compression system, PILC, is proposed to efficiently compress high-quality images using the BPG format at near-lossless standards. PILC integrates domain-specific knowledge and leverages GPU processing power via an end-to-end approach, where its distinct components - encoding, entropy coding, and decoding - are optimized for efficient parallel processing on the GPU. PILC achieves significant compression at near-real-time rates, significantly surpassing existing neural-based systems. Comprehensive experiments and analysis confirm PILC's superiority and provide insight into its strengths and capabilities.

Using 3.0 fb$^{-1}$ of LHCb data at 7 TeV centre-of-mass energy, the $B^{+}$ to $D_s^{+}K^{+}K^{-}$ decay is observed for the first time with a significance of 5.9σ and 3.1σ respectively for the high and low transverse momentum bins initially reported by LHCb. The branching fraction of this decay relative to $B^{+} \to D_s^{+}K^{+}\pi^{-}$ is found to be $r = 0.021 \pm 0.007 \pm 0.001$. Furthermore, the $B^{+}$ to $D_s^{+}\phi$ decay is investigated but not observed, resulting in an upper limit for its branching fraction with $r < 0.15$ being derived from a model-independent analysis.

Optimal transport distances are sensitive to outliers and adversarially introduced noise can lead to spurious equilibria in related problems, such as generative adversarial networks.  To address this issue, we introduce a more resilient variant of optimal transport distances that maintains key properties and is less susceptible to outliers.  The new distances exhibit improved properties like $W_1$-consistency and are capable of detecting noise in problems like regression and classification.

In order to achieve effective collaboration, artificial intelligence agents must demonstrate a deep understanding of their teammates' decision-making processes. This paper introduces a novel learning framework for an AI teammate that learns from its human partner's decision-making structure. By focusing on the underlying decision trees of their partner's strategies, the AI teammate can develop optimal actions to maximize team performance. This framework is tested in a cooperative decision-making task that requires strategic planning and balancing competing goals. Through human-in-the-loop training, the AI teammate can learn to collaborate, leveraging the human partner's decision tree information to make better choices. This paper presents a new approach to learning from human decision-making structures and demonstrates the feasibility of training a collaborative AI teammate using human frameworks.

We examine the dimensions of supersymmetric theories in various spaces, including four, three, and two dimensions. We analyze how the supersymmetry spectrum changes in different four-dimensional theories and use this understanding to predict the dimensions of the N=2, N=3, and N=4 theories. We predict that the N=4 theory lacks new particles beyond the planar limit, supersymmetry constraints in three-dimensional space lead to a finite number of BPS multiplets, and in two-dimensional space, supersymmetry strongly limits the spectrum except for the heavy sector.

To better understand the impact of individual differences on learning visualization skills, we conducted a study comparing the performance and tasks of people from diverse backgrounds. A survey of 100 participants revealed a wide range of professional backgrounds, with no deliberate attempt to select people from various fields. Following a standardized process, we collected data on their performance and tasks, as well as information about their job roles and fields. Based on this research, we categorized the participants' jobs into 11 fields and further grouped them into three main disciplines: science, social science, and business. Our analysis of the data showed that people from the same discipline performed similarly, but those from different disciplines performed at significantly different rates. Interestingly, we found that spatial ability had a greater impact on learning than we initially anticipated, suggesting that people can adapt to new tasks with practice. Finally, we identified a set of tasks that were most challenging for people to complete and proposed a new dataset, V-VISE, which includes these tasks, with the goal of making this dataset publicly available for further research.

We introduce a novel category of loops called clause set loops, which are defined within a vector space framework using clause sets from logic that have been normalised through tautology elimination. It's proven that if a vector space loop exists, it's equivalent to a linear loop. Additionally, for specific logic systems, we identify the necessary and sufficient conditions under which vector space loops can be established. Notably, we find that clause set loops can be defined for various logic systems, including linear logic and untyped lambda calculus.

Graphs of user interactions are becoming a key source for training models to predict future behaviors. Due to their complex structure and the limited availability of data, it's essential to develop graph retrieval techniques that can effectively extract relevant patterns from these graphs. This paper introduces a new model, Entity-Based Graph Embedding, which represents the entire graph on a lower-dimensional representation, allowing for a more accurate and informative retrieval process. By capturing the relationships between entities in the graph, this model enables the retrieval of patterns that would be missed by traditional methods, such as matching item sets or individual entities.

Deep learning models often struggle to learn and generalize effectively when dealing with complex, short-term patterns found in data. To address this challenge, researchers have developed techniques drawing from natural language processing, which have shown promising results in improving model performance in these situations. We introduce a comprehensive overview of these methods, evaluating their efficacy across a range of tasks, and provide an in-depth analysis of how neural networks process and respond to limited data samples. We experiment with these methods on a range of tasks, which require the modeling of short-term data sequences, including predicting system states, learning control policies, and simulating complex dynamics. We assess the impact of these methods on both short-term and long-term data sequences, and investigate their effects on both low-dimensional and high-dimensional data. We also examine the role of neural network size and complexity in influencing the learning process. The results of these experiments demonstrate that these methods can be successfully applied to a variety of problems related to modeling short-term data sequences.

A fair distribution system consists of a central power source and n agents, each one representing a node in a network, which is connected to the source and other nodes, but not to their neighbors. Each node demands a certain amount of electricity and a power source's goal is to distribute the electricity it generates isometrically, ensuring maximum fairness in the distribution, by giving each node its required electricity, while distributing excess power among nodes according to the fairness metric used, which could be maximum total demand, or the minimum total demand of nodes, or the maximum total increase in demand of nodes, or the maximum total increase in demand of nodes, or the maximum total increase in demand of nodes, with the objective of optimizing these fairness metrics.

We introduce the task of and a platform for evaluating event coreference, focusing on identifying related events during the 2020 US presidential election. The event coreference relation means that two events are connected if they share the same occurrence but differ in their topic. The event coreference resolution task is significant for applications such as summarizing debates, analyzing news trends, and tracking public opinion trends. The event coreference relation can be used to recognize co-occurring events, resolve conflicts between events, and uncover underlying connections between seemingly unrelated topics. Our event coreference dataset features annotated events from a limited but highly contentious domain: 2020 US presidential election controversies. The dataset includes event coreference relations between events from the same source and different sources. We also propose a method for automatically generating a dataset based on knowledge graph links between events and their associated entities.

A novel polyhedral representation for the complementarity knapsack set is introduced, comprising a combination of cutting plane representations from both the knapsack and quadratic programming perspectives. This polyhedron is demonstrated to be a valid model for the complementarity knapsack problem, and is shown to be strongly polynomially solvable. Additionally, it is proven that incorporating a specific family of cutting planes results in a polyhedral structure that is close to being complete, with only a single missing family of cuts - that of the quadratic knapsack inequalities.

This paper defines and analyzes the $f\left(X\right)$-Jordan derivation and $f\left(X\right)$-Jordan centralizer of a semiprime algebra, investigating their properties and characterizations, particularly in relation to the function $f\left(X\right)$. We demonstrate that any $f\left(X\right)$-Jordan derivation of a semiprime algebra is a Jordan derivation, and identify the conditions under which an $f\left(X\right)$-Jordan centralizer behaves like a Jordan centralizer. Our results have implications for nonassociative algebras, and provide novel insights into the function $f(X)=1$ in the context of prime algebras.

We derive Weinberg's two-parameter QFT scattering amplitude relations in the
Weinberg sum rule and the Compton scattering amplitude analysis separately, which
are constraints based on helicity representations and spinor products. The two
parameter relations are equivalent to helicity conservation and the s, t,
u channel poles in the Compton scattering amplitude. The analysis shows that the
Compton scattering amplitude and the scattering amplitude sum are dual to each other,
each imposing the other's two parameter relations when evaluated in specific
channels.

We examine a class of families of nonlinear transformations within a Banach space, specifically focusing on those where the transformations' input vectors converge in the norm as the family's index increases without bound. A fundamental property of such families is that they can approximate, in a certain manner, any set of vectors that is bounded and contained within the space. A particular subset of these nonlinear families is composed of linear transformations, which we term transversal families, and we identify and study the characteristics of these nonlinear families that closely resemble transversal families. A key concept in our analysis is that of Favard length, with the Favard length of a bounded set denoting the least number of transformations within a given family that must be applied to any set of vectors within the set. We establish connections between our nonlinear families and generalizations of the Favard length concept, and we derive results that describe and quantify the relationships between these concepts.

We introduce a framework for efficient guided policy search that combines the strengths of imitative learning and model predictive control. The framework starts by using tube MPC to create a resilient tube that estimates the feasible set of a plant under unknown disturbances. An expert policy is then trained using imitative learning within this resilient tube to generate policies that maintain system feasibility under uncertain conditions. The resulting policies can offer robustness guarantees and be easily adapted to new, uncertain systems by simply re-imitating the tube MPC trajectory.

A new concept known as the intrinsic unusual Hall effect (IUHE) has been discovered, which is associated with the chiral anomaly in Weyl semimetals. This phenomenon has garnered significant interest, but its understanding is still limited due to the lack of theoretical explanations. Our study presents a comprehensive semiclassical theory to describe and predict the IUHE at various orders of perturbation. By using this approach, we found that the IUHE can be induced at the third order of perturbation, resulting from the interplay of Berry curvature, Fermi velocity, and the crystallographic momentum. This unusual effect is characterized by a dependence on the applied electric field and is influenced by the specific geometric structure of the Weyl cones. Our findings provide valuable insights into the properties of the IUHE in Weyl semimetals, which can be verified through experiments.

This paper introduces CGDiff, a visual analysis tool that compares variations within a large collection of call graphs, extracted from C++ programs compiled under different compiler versions. CGDiff's innovative design enables the analysis of up to one million call graphs, taking advantage of parallel computing and GPU acceleration. The tool's user-centric approach streamlines common tasks such as call graph comparison, node matching, and node correspondence analysis, with performance not being the only strength, but also high data quality facilitated by CGDiff's automation. CGDiff's effectiveness is demonstrated through four qualitative and quantitative case studies.

The purpose of language modeling is to calculate the probability of a sequence of words, and researchers have typically relied on large datasets of words to achieve this goal. However, one major issue with PMI-based methods is that rare words are often overlooked in favor of more common ones. To address this problem, researchers have been focusing on large datasets that include a wide range of words, including the One Billion Word Benchmark. However, we argue that this approach is flawed because it prioritizes news articles over other types of texts, leading to biased results. To support our claim, we conducted a series of experiments and found that texts from non-newspaper sources actually provide better results on PMI-based language models. Furthermore, we propose a new dataset, the Non-News One Billion Benchmark, which is designed to produce more accurate language models. Our results suggest that these models are better suited for handling out-of-vocabulary words and that the traditional dataset may be limiting the potential of language models in certain applications.

The solar flare's magnetic field and current sheet interact in a complex way, producing various types of oscillations. These oscillations are observed in microwave radiation, specifically through total intensity and polarization properties. Using a specialized code, researchers simulated the behavior of these oscillations in the solar flare's current sheet. The results showed oscillations in total intensity and polarization, as well as a specific pattern of oscillation known as a standing wave. The pattern is caused by the interaction between two types of waves, and can be influenced by the presence of turbulence in the solar plasma. The pattern can be observed in microwave radiation, and can provide insights into the behavior of quasi-periodic oscillations in solar flares. The simulation also showed that the oscillations can be a sign of a current sheet in the solar flare.

This paper introduces a new multi-scale anomaly detection approach for visual quality inspection, which is a crucial step in various manufacturing processes. Traditional methods often rely on pre-defined geometric templates that can be a limitation due to their fixed parameters and inadequate ability to capture intricate shapes. Our proposed solution leverages a compact convolutional network to detect anomalies within images. By employing an efficient algorithm for optimal path detection, it identifies the most suspicious regions within an image. Our approach has been tested on a dataset comprising images of defective and intact components, and the results demonstrate its effectiveness.

New existence proofs are established for certain classes of weak solutions to the KP-I equations in low regularity Sobolev spaces. Specifically, global weak solutions in $H^s(\R^2)$ with $s>5/8$ for the KP-I equations with a general dispersion term are proven to exist and be unique. The validity of these results is further supported by a corresponding uniqueness theorem for weak solutions in more regular Sobolev spaces.

Kramers' theorem establishes the degeneracy of local Hamiltonians with non-zero spin in a magnetic field due to the influence of time-reversal invariance. However, when a quantum system interacts with an environment, Krames' degeneracy can be broken down by a process known as the spin-finding effect. The primary goal of this research is to investigate the restoration of Krames' degeneracy in such systems, where we consider the spin-finding effect as a specific type of environmental interaction. We demonstrate that the Krames' degeneracy is maintained in a particular regime of the system's interaction with its environment, where we define this regime using the strength of the system's interaction and the rate at which it approaches thermal equilibrium with its environment. We further show that the Krames' degeneracy is preserved under specific conditions of detailed balance, where we consider various types of system-environment interactions.

In highly-mobile millimeter-wave MIMO systems, accurately predicting future channel state information (CSI) responses becomes increasingly challenging due to rapid changes in position and environment. To address this issue, we develop a two-stage deep learning framework, consisting of a global network and multiple local networks, which enables efficient CSI prediction even with minimal training data. The global network provides a general understanding of the signal characteristics, while the local networks adapt to the specific conditions of each CSI sample. By using a deep neural network to calculate the difference between the predicted and actual CSI responses, we significantly reduce the estimation error. Furthermore, we employ a data augmentation technique to improve the accuracy of the neural networks by transforming the 3D spatial coordinates into a single feature vector. Through extensive simulations, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method in real-world scenarios.

This paper presents a novel non-parametric approach for calculating inequality metrics in small data sets. It introduces a mixture of Beta distribution as a data augmentation method to reduce bias in inequality estimates derived from inequality indices. We show that this method's bias is directly proportional to the number of support points in the data, and that it can be significantly reduced with as few as three to five support points. Furthermore, the method's asymptotic variance is comparable to that of a parametric maximum likelihood estimator. We also develop a small sample bootstrap method to calculate asymptotic standard errors and conduct Monte Carlo simulations and real-world applications to evaluate the efficacy of the proposed method.

We calculate the scaling approximation of the Szegö kernel on complex manifolds featuring a Kaehler metric with nonnegative holomorphic sectional curvature. These manifolds are classified into two types: those embedded in complex space, and those described by a family of Hermitian line bundles of fixed degree. In both cases, the Szegö kernel has a smooth section over the Grauert cylinder, and our analysis yields a scaling approximation in terms of asymptotic expansions. We apply this to the scalar curvature of the Grauert metric, which allows us to recover previously known results for the scalar curvature of the Fubini-Study metric on projective space.

This paper presents a new approach to generating a reverse line graph (RLG) from a given line graph (LG) or its dual. The proposed method, called the Matrix Relabeling Algorithm (MARINLINGA), is an improvement on previously established algorithms, including the one developed by Y.A. Roussopoulos in 1983, as reported in 'On Line Graph Problems in the Framework of Query Optimization'. Unlike Roussopoulos's algorithm, MARINLINGA does not require an adjacency matrix, making it more versatile and efficient. Instead, it utilizes a list of edge endpoints and their respective indices to construct the RLG edge list directly. This allows MARINLINGA to handle graphs with zero-degree vertices, which are not supported by Roussopoulos's algorithm. Furthermore, MARINLINGA offers a concise and efficient implementation that outperforms Roussopoulos's algorithm in terms of time complexity, especially when dealing with large-scale graphs.

This paper validates a hypothesis proposed by Lee-Lee, concerning a connection between the S2 condition and Gorenstein flatness for modules over a Gorenstein ring A, by establishing an equivalence of categories between the category of S2 injective modules and that of Gorenstein injective modules.

Our analysis of 12 prominent Java libraries and their dependencies reveals
significant weight gain in popular projects, particularly Java Central Compact, 
with a 67% rise in specific dependencies and 24% overall increase between 
2018 and 2022. Our research shows that nearly three-quarters of a project's 
dependencies don't directly contribute to its main features, and only 33% 
of'Compact' library dependencies are used in a given period. Our study 
highlights the value of our automated dependency analysis tool and suggests 
strategies to minimize dependency mass, such as regularly updating dependencies, 
prioritizing dependency removal, and implementing a dependency migration plan.

In this research, we investigate the interplay between three distinct types of entangled biphoton states, which are represented as chains with different lengths. We examine how the relationships between these states, which can be controlled through a quantum circuit, evolve over time. The relationships between the states, which can be described as familial connections, reveal how the length of these connections impacts the overall entanglement of the system. The findings suggest that shorter, more complex connections tend to dominate the longer, more straightforward connections. The control parameters also exhibit non-classical behavior, which is a result of the unique interplay between the states, rather than a property inherent to the parameters themselves.

In decision-making under uncertainty, particularly with multiple stages and risk considerations, determining the most effective scenarios is crucial. However, the task of identifying the most critical situations in problems involving variations in uncertainty is complex. To address this issue, we develop a method to identify the most effective scenarios in problems involving variations in uncertainty by minimizing the impact of such variations. Our approach relies on a specific type of calculation that considers the differences in uncertainty, which allows us to identify the most effective scenarios in a given problem. We apply this method to different types of problems, including those with limited and multiple resources, and demonstrate its effectiveness in identifying the most efficient solutions.

Our proposed system predicts the next action in a sequence by utilizing a deep learning framework. To address the limitations of traditional action prediction methods, we introduce a new model that can effectively handle rare and novel actions using a complex feature mapping layer. This feature mapping layer is equipped with a radial basis function kernel, enabling it to transform low-dimensional features into a high-dimensional space, making it easier to identify actions. This approach not only learns to recognize frequent actions but also recognizes less frequent actions, ultimately enhancing the overall accuracy of the system. We validate the efficacy of our method through experiments on two datasets, demonstrating its ability to outperform existing benchmarks.

We introduce a novel framework for achieving deep thermalization in quantum systems, encompassing both isolated and system-environment integrated models. Our approach is characterized by adjustable, controllable parameters that enable tailored design times for inducing thermalization in specific subsystems. By leveraging these parameters, we formulate a set of self-consistent equations that capture the internal dynamics within the subsystems. These equations are derived from the system's microscopic description and provide a unified framework for analyzing diverse scenarios, including the Gross-Pitaevskii model, the XY model, and the spin-boson model.

We investigate the properties of uniform trees using a real parameter $\gamma \ge 0$, which is a modified version of the metric tree structure's Laplacian, denoted as $\mathcal{D}^2_\gamma(T)$. The research focuses on the boundedness of this operator within various function spaces and their Fourier transforms, including a demonstration that its Fourier multiplier fails to be a bounded symbol when $\gamma > 1$. Additionally, we examine the nuclearity and nullity of $\mathcal{D}^2_\gamma(T)$, specifically showing it's a non-nuclear operator for any $\gamma > 0$. The research further explores the composition properties of $\mathcal{D}^2_\gamma(T)$ and its connection to the standard Laplacian $\Delta_T$ for uniform trees. The findings indicate that the composition of $\mathcal{D}^2_\gamma(T)$ and another operator shares a similar structure to the composition of the standard Laplacian and another operator.

The widespread adoption of mobile devices has led to a significant increase in cellular traffic, prompting the development of the fifth generation (5G) mobile network. The 5G specifications, established by 3GPP, have introduced several new features, such as multi-input multiple-output antennas, beamforming, multiple-input single-output, multiple antenna configurations, multiple carrier aggregation schemes, and multiple access schemes, with the aim of enhancing the performance of 5G networks. This research paper presents an experimental evaluation of 5G networks, utilizing a testbed consisting of multiple USim-enabled smartphones, connected to a software-defined radio base station and various core nodes, allowing for the assessment of 5G functionalities, including multi-RATs, data transfer, and VoLTE capabilities, in different environments. The findings indicate that smartphones are the most suitable choice for testing 5G networks, particularly in scenarios where active mobile connections are required.

Deep neural networks often overestimate their predictions for out-of-distribution inputs, which can be mitigated by employing a novel approach called CODES. This approach identifies and isolates minor classes within a dataset, trains a Chamfer-based network on these classes, and uses this network to provide a confidence score for out-of-distribution instances. We demonstrate that CODES outperforms existing methods in terms of both accuracy and confidence calibration on various benchmark datasets. Additionally, our code can be accessed through the following repository: https://github.com/zhenghui-chen/codes

The CMS experiment at the LHC has analyzed pp collisions at 13 TeV, examining the development of collective behavior in high-energy events characterized by 2, 3, and 4 jets. The study focuses on the angular relationships between jets within an absolute pseudorapidity range of 2.40 to 4.19, and between the second-highest and highest transverse momentum particles in events with 2 and 3 jets. The data reveals a notable increase in jet correlations at high transverse momenta, and lower angular separations, in events with 4 jets compared to those with fewer jets.

Deep learning models have achieved remarkable success in computer vision tasks, 
but their applications are often hindered by the need for a substantial amount 
of labeled data. This limitation is particularly problematic in settings where 
data is scarce, and labeling it becomes cost-prohibitive. This challenge has 
given rise to the development of semi-supervised learning methods that combine 
small datasets with manual labels and large amounts of unlabeled data. These 
approaches have been instrumental in creating highly effective deep learning 
models for computer vision applications. This survey provides an in-depth analysis 
of semi-supervised learning, its connection to unsupervised learning, and offers 
a comprehensive overview of the current state-of-the-art research in this domain.

Identifying anomalies in datasets has become increasingly crucial across various fields, but current state-of-the-art methods often struggle with robustness and adaptability. These limitations arise due to their reliance on domain-specific parameters and inability to handle missing values. A new approach, RECol, leverages the concept of data reconstruction error to detect anomalies by iteratively removing rows with minimal error. This method yields a consistent linear time complexity, is free from domain-specific parameters, and effectively handles missing values. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate that RECol not only rivals the performance of existing top-rated methods but also exhibits greater resilience against parameter variations. Additionally, our results show that RECol performs exceptionally well in scenarios characterized by small to moderate anomalies, significantly outperforming more complex models.

We establish the existence of a single, uniformly integrable solution to a nonlinear equation representing the dynamics of a stochastic process. This process is defined as a time-invariant, additive functional integral with non-linear coefficients influenced by a Wiener process and a compensated Poisson random measure. The solution's integrability is tied to the dimensions of the noise and the nonlinearity classes. The proof is grounded in the weak-convergence concept and the compactness of the probability measures within an appropriate Banovà space. The solution's properties are leveraged to demonstrate the non-linear mixing and ergodic properties of the stochastic process in question.

The potential for significant new findings on neutrino properties in the next decade
paves the way for a series of precise measurements that could lead to a substantial
reduction in the current knowledge limitations. One area where substantial progress
can be made is in the evaluation of the neutrino mass and mixing parameters, a key
focus area for the future neutrino oscillation experiments. Another crucial aspect
involves determining the properties of the neutrino, specifically its electric charge,
magnetic moment, and the effects of radiation pressure and self-interaction. This
article examines the current state of the neutrino magnetic moment, a key parameter in
the field, with the current upper limit being around $3\times 10^{-13} \, \mu_\text{N} \,
(\text{90\% confidence level})$. We also explore the possibilities for lowering this
limit through various experimental methods. Furthermore, we discuss the potential for
the discovery of neutrino dark matter, a hypothetical particle that could be a dark
matter candidate, and the effects of neutrino dark matter on neutrino flavor oscillations
and the cosmic microwave background radiation.

A synchronized oscillation of neurons, known as a rhythmic brain activity, can be observed in various brain functions, such as sleep cycles and motor control.  In studying this phenomenon, researchers have identified two key factors: excitatory neurons, which promote activity, and inhibitory glial cells, which help regulate activity levels.  A model of the neuron-glial network, first introduced in 2012, incorporates both of these elements and has been shown to exhibit rhythmic activity through computer simulations.  This paper will explore the different mechanisms behind this rhythmic behavior, examining multiple scenarios in which it can arise.

A theoretical model of a neutral particle with spin one-half is analyzed within a combined electromagnetic field, consisting of a uniform external magnetic field and fluctuations of the electromagnetic field. This analysis reveals that the topological characteristics of the particle's energy spectrum are exposed, enabling the calculation of its topological charges tied to the magnetic field's configurations - the Skyrmion current and non-Abelian Chern-Pontryagin density. The results indicate a direct relationship between these topological invariants and the Berry phase accumulated by the particle in response to the magnetic field.

A new, universal approach to simulating the expansion of a boundary in a complex system is presented, where particles are constantly arriving at the boundary from an outside source, influencing its size through interactions. The simulation is based on a novel, first-departure-driven recursion formula that considers the initial and final behaviors of particles as they leave the boundary for the very first time. The recursion formula is derived from a combination of two key elements: a first-departure-driven master equation and a first-departure-driven Laplace transform. The simulation is applied to a variety of scenarios, including a queueing system, a queue with waiting areas, a financial market model, and a model of interacting particles. The simulation is shown to accurately predict the size of these systems after a certain period, matching or exceeding the accuracy of traditional methods.

J. Cheung introduced the concept of a hyperbolic link being a member of a particular category of semigroups. This paper delves into understanding properties of such links, focusing on Cheung's Hyperbolic L-space Links and establishing the connection between them and semigroups. It specifically identifies characteristics of hyperbolic L-space links through their associated semigroup properties, as well as exploring the role of these links in the context of hyperbolic geometry.

We propose a new approach to deriving non-equilibrium hydrodynamics from kinetic theory using a non-uniform entropy concept. This method involves constructing a Poisson map that maintains a positivity constraint. Under the condition of small gradients, our proposed system exhibits a hyperbolic nature and satisfies a non-uniform entropy equation, ultimately giving rise to a non-equilibrium hydrodynamic framework. This non-uniform entropy framework is applicable to both ideal and viscous fluids, and in the limit of vanishing viscosity, it converges to a well-known Poisson-type fluid dynamics. Furthermore, our proposed method can be applied to various kinetic theories, such as the Boltzmann equation and the Bhatnagar-Gross-Krook equation, as demonstrated by a specific example using the Boltzmann equation.

The use of deep learning-based methods for identifying artifacts in endoscopic video streams has been explored, but their reliability in real-world settings remains uncertain. This study investigates the potential of combining the outputs of diverse deep learning models to enhance the accuracy and robustness of this approach. A dataset of endoscopic video sequences with artificial artifacts was compiled, and the performance of both individual and ensemble-based methods was evaluated using different metrics. The results indicate that ensembling can improve the detection of artifacts in frames, as well as overall video quality.

Research into the underlying structure of source code has led to numerous studies examining specific characteristics, including the use of context-free grammars to identify patterns. Our investigation into the structure of identifiers in source code found that they can be represented by a large set of context-free grammar patterns, with each element having a specific meaning. To develop a comprehensive understanding, we created a dataset of these patterns, analyzed their distribution, and investigated their relationship with programming tasks. Our findings suggest that these patterns are widespread and can be categorized into meaningful categories, with each one associated with a specific function.

This paper introduces a novel infinite-dimensional $\square_q$-module, drawing from the $q$-shuffle subalgebra in the affine $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ setting. This module can be constructed using a power series-based framework, and we demonstrate that it adheres to a specific $\square_q$-Module Property.

The evolution of polycrystalline microstructures in materials is heavily influenced by the growth of grains, which, in turn, affects the final properties of the material. To gain a deeper understanding of this process, researchers have developed a data-driven approach to analyze the growth kinetics of grains in complex systems. By applying this method to data from various sources, including experiments and simulations, researchers can gain insight into the underlying dynamics of grain growth. A comprehensive database of grain-growth kinetics in different systems has been created, revealing patterns and trends that were previously unknown. Furthermore, this method can be used to predict the growth rates of grains in new systems, even when limited data is available. The data-driven approach has the potential to be applied to a wide range of materials, including those used in aerospace and energy production, and can also be used to inform the development of new materials.

Estimating human pose and shape from a single image has been a focal point 
of the research community's efforts. Despite considerable progress, existing 
evaluations primarily concentrate on methodical investigations, with less 
emphasis on the impact of benchmark datasets. In this paper, we introduce the 
first comprehensive evaluation of the influence of benchmark datasets on the 
categorical performance of state-of-the-art methods for estimating human pose 
and shape from a single image. Our analysis reveals that the performance 
varies significantly across datasets, with some being highly competitive, 
others failing to produce results, and a few being detrimental. Our findings 
highlight the importance of developing benchmark datasets that are well-aligned 
with the goals of the underlying research question.

In the context of strong electron-electron attraction, the potential for superconductivity is analyzed in a discrete system consisting of sparse, non-interacting sites. Using the Bogoliubov transformation method, the exact solution for the energy of a two-site system reveals a state with equal spin and charge densities, characteristic of Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer-like pairing. Notably, the conditions for a mesoscopic superconductivity phenomenon are discussed, suggesting it may occur under certain conditions in systems with a limited number of sites.

We have developed a comprehensive framework for converting theoretical models into a unified format, focusing on leptoquarks that interact with standard model particles. This system is designed to be flexible and adaptable to various theories, allowing for the easy comparison and integration of different models. We have applied our framework to several scenarios, including both minimal and extended versions of leptoquark models, demonstrating their potential to simplify and standardize the process of theoretical matching.

The concept of a category in mathematics holds significant weight, influencing numerous abstract structures. In the realm of machine learning, categories serve as an essential abstraction, with numerous notable applications. This paper delves into the applications of categories within machine learning, positioning them as an overarching framework for understanding the field. Additionally, it provides an examination of the learning process as a category, offering a fresh perspective on subjects like online learning and Bayesian inference, and highlighting areas for further research.

This research paper explores the terminal sliding-mode (TSM) control method for a second-order motion system. By redefining the traditional TSM approach, an improved algorithm is developed which eliminates the non-singular matrix issue and achieves faster convergence without settling time restrictions. Comparative simulations in both continuous-time and discrete-time domains demonstrate the superiority of the revised control method under various conditions, including disturbance presence, when compared to the original TSM approach and other variants such as the augmented TSM (ATSM) and non-singular TSM (NSTSM).

This study introduces a pioneering non-destructive technique utilizing ultrasonic resonance to quantify the internal organization of lithium-ion and other prismatic batteries. Leveraging the principles of resonating rectangular boxes, the proposed method enables precise measurements of cell dimensions and can potentially identify the presence of layers within electrode materials. Building upon this foundation, we have developed a novel approach to estimate the volume of active layers within positive and negative cells based on layer thickness and number. Using this technique, we have analyzed the changes in layer thickness and volume over 100 charge-discharge cycles, determining the maximum capacity loss during aging. Additionally, we have employed our method to investigate the internal structure of different lithium-ion cells and have identified the layer thickness range within their electrodes.

This research introduces a novel approach to solving control problems for complex systems with a limited time span, known as discrete-time flat systems. The proposed method leverages the system's flatness function to efficiently design and implement control strategies. The approach's effectiveness is demonstrated through a simulation of a gantry crane system. The developed controller is then compared to a conventional flatness-based controller under similar operating conditions. The key advantage of the new method lies in its ability to produce a shorter transition period and reduce control efforts.

Image-Caption models struggle with noisy labels, particularly when training on human-provided, mismatched captions. These mislabeled captions (like repetitive words or phrases) can negatively affect the entire system. To address this issue, we've developed a novel training method called Cooperative Distillation, which separates image and text information to minimize noise. By using a multi-view graph network to extract relevant features, we can then distill these features in a cooperative manner, enhancing the accuracy of image and text descriptions. Experimental results on the MSCOCO dataset demonstrate our method's superiority, with notable improvements in performance.

A subset of strings over a finite alphabet is termed well-linked if the string concatenation of n copies of the subset forms a connected string under the concatenation operation, and the number of strings should be at least the minimum degree of the resulting graph when the concatenation is viewed as an edge between strings. We investigate properties of well-linked subsets and introduce the concept of the well-linked number of a string, representing the maximum number of well-linked subsets containing the string. We also establish a relationship between this value and the number of spanning trees in a modified version of a well-known graph transformation. Furthermore, we show that this value is at most the number of strings in any subset containing the string, and that it is also bounded by the sum of the values of well-linked subsets of the string's length minus one, while providing a lower bound through the concatenation of strings of the string, followed by the application of another well-known graph transformation. We also demonstrate that this value is at most the number of strings in any subset containing the string, and that it is also bounded by the sum of the values of the well-linked subsets of the string's length minus one, while providing a lower bound through the concatenation of strings of the string, followed by the application of another well-known graph transformation.

A specific type of category is referred to as an Ehresmann category if it can be visually represented as a graph whose connections form a group. The graph in question is referred to as a grey category, and the study of these categories is rooted in the work of A. Connes and M. Connes. The focus of this research paper is on ordered Ehresmann categories, where the connections also adhere to a specific ordering. The authors derive a method for simplifying these categories, reveal their inherent structure, and demonstrate that they can be represented as a combination of simpler categories. The results from this research can be extended to include ordered monoids and provide a new understanding of their category counterparts. The authors also explore the connections between these categories and develop a method for categorifying the process of taking the product of two monoids.

Self-attention is a key component in current natural language processing models, enabling the modeling of complex relationships within data. Research has shown that increasing the depth of self-attention networks leads to enhanced performance, yet this comes at a significant computational cost. A crucial aspect to be explored is how to balance depth and width in self-attention networks to achieve optimal results, particularly since the relationship between the two is not well understood. In this research, we investigate the interaction between depth and width in self-attention networks and demonstrate that increasing depth can be replicated by expanding width, thereby reducing computational complexity. Our findings are based on empirical evidence, and we support this approach by examining the attention patterns of the networks through both theoretical and experimental methods.

The text reports the low-temperature synthesis of BiFeO$_3$ nanoparticles with enhanced magnetization and notable photocatalytic efficiency in dye degradation and hydrogen production. The low-temperature processing was achieved through a sol-gel method, where bismuth oxide and iron oxide were used as precursors, at a 1:0.1 precursor ratio, yielding a hexagonal phase at 600 degrees Celsius. The resulting material exhibited a significant increase in magnetization when iron content was elevated, as well as a notable reduction in the hydrogen production volume when the ratio was increased to 1:0.5. The material's efficiency in both dye degradation and hydrogen production was found to be directly related to its surface area, with the optimal conditions for these processes being achieved at 80 degrees Celsius. The text also presents a comparative study of the material's performance in relation to different temperatures and the hydrogen volume.

We are investigating the theoretical implications of a ${\rm SU}(6)$ flavor framework, where the bottom quark and tau lepton are composite entities made up of two fundamental constituents, denoted as $b_1$ and $b_2$, and $\tau_1$ and $\tau_2$ respectively. The mass determinants for these particles are calculated within this framework, where $b$ and $\tau$ are found to be composite in a specific mass range, suggesting that the top quark and muon could be modeled in a similar way. The hypothesis is that the fundamental constituents, $b_1, b_2, \tau_1,$ and $\tau_2$, are Majorana particles, where the interactions between them are mediated by a flavor-conserving gauge boson, $Z_*$, and a flavor-violating gauge boson, $g_*$, resulting in a flavor structure similar to that of the Standard Model.

This paper addresses a critical challenge in understanding and synthesizing three-dimensional visual information. We focus on a practical application, where a robotic hand or hand-like device is used to interact with objects in a 3D space. We propose a novel approach to estimate an object's shape and position within a 3D volume based on 2D images captured through a camera. Our method leverages a deep neural network that generates 3D coordinates of an object's surface by processing images from different viewpoints. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through a series of experiments, which show that our method outperforms existing alternatives in terms of accuracy and reliability. We evaluate our method under various conditions, including object size, camera angle, and image quality. We also compare the performance of our method against alternative methods that rely on different assumptions and models. Our results indicate that our approach achieves the best results in terms of accuracy and robustness.

The Ca-K index serves as a vital solar parameter that measures the level of activity on the sun. This index directly correlates with the characteristics of the sun like solar irradiance, solar wind, and magnetic field. Consequently, tracking the Ca-K index over time enables researchers to study long-term solar activity patterns. Historically, the Ca-K index data have been recorded at Kodaikanan Observatory since 1952. This study leverages this extensive dataset spanning over a century to examine long-term patterns in the Ca-K index and its relationship with various solar features. Furthermore, it aims to establish a correlation between the Ca-K index and magnetic field strength, sunspot area, sunspot index, and magnetic flux.

The first experimental findings of the $\Sigma^+ \to p \mu^+ \mu^-$ decay have been obtained using $4.3$ fb$^{-1}$ of $pp$ collision data recorded by the LHCb detector at centre-of-mass energies of $7$ TeV and $8$ TeV. The observed data exhibits a significant discrepancy from background expectations, yielding a $3.8\sigma$ statistical importance. Considering systematic uncertainties, it translates to a $3.4\sigma$ discovery significance. The observed mass of the decay is $1.78 \pm 0.17^{+0.10}_{-0.11}$ GeV/c$^2$, with a forward-backward asymmetry of $-0.077 \pm 0.077^{+0.077}_{-0.070}$, indicating potential contributions from $\Sigma(1670)$ or $\Sigma(1940)$ resonances.

A novel distributed approach for evaluating Symbolic Manipulation Tasks (SMTs) is introduced, where complex mathematical expressions are divided into manageable components and assigned to network nodes for processing. By employing test-depth partitioning, this distribution method leverages the efficiency of symbolic mathematics libraries, facilitating seamless task distribution and overlap detection. The proposed method is compatible with various distributed architectures, including a hybrid cloud model, and is demonstrated on a 100-node hybrid cloud network. The results indicate that distributed assessment of SMTs can be accomplished efficiently, with the proposed method capable of achieving significant speedup compared to a single-machine implementation.

The magnetic relaxation in a specific group of arranged magnetic nanoparticles is examined, focusing on the effects of temperature, anisotropic energy, and inter-particle interaction. The study considers both the first-order and second-order transitions in the context of the Monte Carlo method, revealing that these effects can be accurately represented by specific power-law laws when a certain threshold is exceeded. The research also explores the relationship between these results and recent findings concerning the same sequence of events without the presence of anisotropic energy.

Federated learning (FL) enables training models on distributed data without
exposing it, without the central server having access to the data. However,
the central server retains control over model updates and acts as a
single-point-of-failure, making it a potential target for attacks. In this study,
we introduce FedFree, a distributed FL approach that eliminates reliance on
a central server. FedFree achieves this by having clients proactively
determining their local models using only single-sided trust, and by utilizing
a global model that is directly managed by the clients. We also present an
efficient strategy for dynamically adjusting the number of clients involved in
the process, and our analysis indicates that FedFree significantly reduces
the computational burden of the central server. Our experiments show that
FedFree successfully eliminates the need for a central server while
maintaining performance comparable to traditional FL approaches.

Short-text classification is a fundamental challenge in natural language processing and computer vision. We introduce a method for categorizing sequential short texts, leveraging recurrent and convolution neural networks. Our approach combines features extracted from recurrent neural networks with those from convolution neural networks to accurately determine the category of a given short text. We evaluate our model on Twitter data, achieving notable success with a significant lead over current state-of-the-art methods.

The telecentric etalon, an extension of the standard Fabry-P\'erot etalon, has been extensively researched in the field of laser technology. It is characterized by a reflective boundary with a telecentric phase center aligned with the light source and a specific point behind the etalon. This study introduces an analytical model for the telecentric etalon, incorporating both its transfer function and frequency response. This comprehensive model is applied to the analysis of various optical devices, such as laser resonators, laser sensors, and interferometers. It is particularly useful for simplifying the design and analysis of these devices, and has been previously utilized to study the etalon-based optical sensor.

A system for matching entities is considered consistent if it allocates the same entity to a given set of entities the same number of times for all entities.
