This research examines the subdifferential of the combined numerical radius, denoted as $w_{\rm c}(A)$. It is demonstrated that for any normal operator on a complex Hilbert space, the subdifferential of $w_{\rm c}(A)$ is equivalent to the set of bounded linear operators $B$, where the inequality $|w_{\rm c}(A+B)| + |w_{\rm c}(AB)| \le w_{\rm c}(A)^2 + |w_{\rm c}(A)|^2$ holds true. Additionally, we derive the subdifferential of the combined numerical radius for specific operator classes, specifically, we show that for any bounded operator on a complex Hilbert space, the subdifferential of $w_{\rm c}(A)$ forms a closed operator, and for any normal operator on a complex Hilbert space, the subdifferential of $w_{\rm c}(A)$ corresponds to the set of bounded linear operators $B$, satisfying a specific inequality.

The concept of differential privacy has gained significant attention in recent years due to its ability to ensure the confidentiality of protected data. Various applications of differential privacy have been developed to cater to diverse needs. In the financial sector, data privacy is a critical concern, and differential privacy can be utilized to address this issue effectively. In this paper, a novel privacy-preserving framework for financial transactions is proposed, and its privacy guarantee is ensured using a rigorous analysis based on the R\'{e}nyi divergence. The framework's efficiency is evaluated by measuring the R\'{e}nyi divergence and the distortion error, and it is also shown to be robust against model perturbations. The framework's practicality is further demonstrated through its implementation using real-world financial data, and the experimental results confirm its effectiveness.

This research paper explores the stochastic mappings and random dispersion fields approach, correlating these concepts with established theories, particularly stochastic processes, random walks, and fractional Brownian motions. The study focuses on the stochastic mappings framework, examining the properties of a unique class of such mappings and their inherent fractional Brownian motion, as well as the inherent stochastic process associated with random dispersion fields. The investigation also delves into the relationships between the stochastic mappings and their corresponding diffusion processes, including the derivation of the associated stochastic differential equations. Additionally, the paper examines the general case of itineraries in stochastic mappings and their connections to Markov chains and itineraries in symbolic sequences.

Research on hydrogen safety and energy production has driven the study of hydrogen mixtures compressed to high pressures and temperatures, which are susceptible to combustion. To better understand these conditions, researchers have been using high-speed imaging techniques to observe the behavior of hydrogen mixtures under various conditions. A laser system with a duration of approximately 10 nanoseconds was employed to initiate combustion in a 0.2 bar hydrogen mixture with 9.5% oxygen content at a pressure of 50 bar, while optical imaging was used to capture the behavior of hot gas bubbles formed during combustion. The results showed that hot gas bubbles formed within 1 millisecond, which then expanded rapidly, reaching speeds of 100 meters per second, and exhibited a spherical shape. The findings also indicated that the behavior of hot gas bubbles in hydrogen mixtures is similar to that of hot gas bubbles in other combustible gases, which could aid in understanding combustion dynamics in such mixtures.

Recent breakthroughs in deep learning have driven significant advancements in image segmentation, with attention mechanisms now being widely applied to enhance segmentation accuracy. However, existing methods primarily focus on detailed feature analysis within images, often neglecting the crucial information provided by the surrounding context. This context is vital for establishing precise object boundaries, which remains a major challenge in traditional segmentation techniques. To bridge this gap, a new boundary-aware segmentation network is introduced in this paper, designed to effectively leverage the surrounding context and enhance segmentation performance. The proposed method is optimized for efficient processing on mobile and web platforms, with its code and implementation made publicly available.

This research introduces a driver messenger system, enabling communication exchange between drivers through a social networking platform. The system's core feature involves one driver sending self-recorded video clips along with a written or spoken lane change intention, which the recipient driver can receive and interpret in their vehicle. The paper outlines the development of this social networking-inspired system, highlighting its implementation details, user findings and implications. The messenger's functionality is explored, as well as the consideration of various design elements, including user comfort, data protection and potential conflicts.

The movement of non-interacting particles in space is influenced by their inherent velocity, leading to a non-random distribution of the particles. This can result in particles accumulating at specific points or along particular paths within the space. In this research, we explore the effect of boundaries on a container with active particles using various shapes and sizes, and no external forces at play. This study is relevant to systems such as bacterial swarming, and the self-organization of microorganisms.

The average particle model is often used to analyze nuclear structure and reactions involving collective behavior. However, this model has a limitation when it comes to Siegert states, which it cannot accurately predict. Researchers have proposed a new approach to enhance the average particle model, suggesting that fluctuations in Siegert states can be described by a part of the nuclear wave function that does not belong to the single-particle basis. This idea is based on the assumption that Siegert states have a small overlap with the single-particle basis. By incorporating this additional component, the model's average particle wave function can be modified to include Siegert states, even when the single-particle model is not applicable. As a result, the model's energy spectrum can be refined to include not only collective modes but also some Siegert states, which are difficult to distinguish from collective modes.

Observations of the Si IV 1390-1415 nm line in a solar flare made using the Interface Region Imaging Spectrograph have revealed rapid post-flare darkening of spectral profiles, which occurred within a short time frame of 0.6-1.7 seconds. These changes were observed in both the leading and trailing edges of the spectral profiles, and are attributed to a decrease in electron density at high-temperature coronal loops. This phenomenon is consistent with other rapid changes recently reported in the He I 1083 nm and Ca XVIII 193 nm lines. It is suggested that these changes may be caused by a process known as beam-smoothing, which is influenced by the density of the coronal plasma.

The strong CP problem, tied to the neutron electric dipole moment, and the dark matter axion, all share a common origin. In this context, we explore the strong CP problem and the neutron electric dipole moment under the assumption that the QCD axion solves the strong CP problem. Utilizing a generalized potential for the axion field, $a$, we derive a general expression for the neutron EDM, $d_n$, which is valid for an axion in a generic external magnetic field. The analysis reveals that the neutron EDM is predominantly influenced by the axion mass, $m_a$, and the axion potential's higher-order terms. The results suggest that the presence of an axion in a magnetic field causes the neutron spin to precess, leading to an EDM of $d_n \propto \langle a \rangle$ in the absence of the axion potential. The precession effect is particularly pronounced in the presence of the axion potential, where the neutron spin experiences a non-linear precession. This non-linear precession results in a neutron EDM that is proportional to the axion potential's higher-order terms and the axion field strength. The analysis further reveals that the axion potential's higher-order terms can be constrained by the limits on the neutron electric dipole moment, particularly in the axion mass range of $10^{-22}$ eV. The results suggest that the constraints on the axion potential's higher-order terms can be significantly tightened by future measurements

A detailed analysis of the collision cascade process in low-energy irradiation events is conducted to examine its impact on the critical angle of self-organized patterns in thin films. The study focuses on the spatial distribution of displaced atoms within the film, taking into account both the atom's vertical and horizontal momentum. For low energies, the impact of displaced atoms on the critical angle is contingent upon their ability to reach the film's surface. A key finding is that atoms experiencing multiple collisions during their trajectory, particularly those with lateral displacement, have a greater likelihood of reaching the surface. The study reveals that the atom's surface arrival probability is influenced by the maximum depth of their displacement, as well as their horizontal momentum loss. A critical threshold is identified, below which the atom's horizontal momentum is insufficient to prevent it from returning to the film's surface. The study's results demonstrate that the introduction of a critical angle threshold for self-organization in low-energy irradiation events is contingent upon the presence of a minimum horizontal momentum, $p_{\rm min}$, which varies with the irradiation dose.

In software engineering, code duplication within programs is a significant problem. This occurs when developers copy and modify existing source codes instead of thoroughly understanding and adapting them, resulting in unintentional plagiarism. An anti-plagiarism tool is proposed to detect and eliminate such copied code segments by providing a clear comparison with the original code. The anti-plagiarism tool is designed to guide developers in comprehending the modified code in relation to the original. A novel approach to code duplication detection is introduced, which utilizes the path approach to identify and quantify the level of similarity between two programs. The path approach is based on the idea that during manual code modification, developers fail to change all aspects of the original code, leaving behind similarities. By comparing the control-flow graphs of the original and modified programs, the proposed approach can identify and eliminate code duplication, providing a clear comparison with the original code. The proposed method is implemented in C# and applied to real-world programs, demonstrating its effectiveness in detecting and eliminating code duplication.

Consider a family of non-Euclidean functions on a specific type of complex plane defined by a certain value. We analyze the behavior of series that combine these functions raised to any degree, with the series summing infinitely many terms defined by a complex number's properties. We identify conditions under which this series will eventually consistently surpass a given complex number's value, with specific conditions involving the size of the series' terms, the degree at which they are raised, and a measure of their variability. These conditions are more relaxed when certain terms are square roots of other functions within the family, with additional requirements involving the size of the series' terms, the degree at which they are raised, and a measure of their variability. We identify conditions under which this series will consistently surpass a given complex number's value, with specific conditions involving the size of the series' terms, the degree at which they are raised, and a measure of their variability.

This note addresses the metric version of a classical question regarding near subgroups, specifically answering the question in the context of free groups. Furthermore, we resolve two related problems of Mandel's work from 1984: If $G$ is a group with $\Phi(G)$ is a near subgroup of $G$, then is $\Phi(G)$ a quasiconjugacy class in $G$? Additionally, if $\Phi(G)$ is a near subgroup of $G$, then is $\Phi(G)$ a quasiconjugacy class in $G$ or is $\Phi(G)$ a virtually abelian subgroup? Our positive answer to these questions builds upon a key finding that in a free group, any metric near subgroup is a quasiconjugacy class or contains a virtually abelian subgroup of infinite index.

We introduce a numerical system for determining the greatest log-concave probability density in a specified set. This set can be defined by a set of linear inequalities, making it a convex convex-concave function. This type of function is known to have a unique concave solution for any convex objective function. We have developed an algorithm that efficiently solves these types of problems, and it has a proven time complexity of O(n^2 * log(n)) for problems in n-dimensional space. We have also created a program that implements this algorithm, and it can handle much larger data sets. This program can identify the probability density in a specified set, and it can also be used to find the probability density in a specified set that is close to a given probability density.

Sampling configurations of granular systems using the Wang-Landau algorithm can efficiently explore configuration space. By treating granular particles as indistinguishable units, the algorithm can produce equilibrium configurations based on an entropy calculation. This approach samples configurations according to their volume occupation, thereby facilitating the analysis of granular packings' entropy. By combining the Wang-Landau algorithm with a volume-based approach, it's possible to derive and estimate the partition function of a granular system, enabling the calculation of thermodynamic properties such as entropy and free energy. This method was successfully applied to a 2D packing of disks to demonstrate its capabilities in analyzing and estimating the configurational entropy of granular systems.

We investigate a zero-sum game set on graphs, where one player has complete control over a graph's vertices. The other player aims to maximize a weighted sum of vertices from a predetermined subset, achieved by strategically removing vertices to limit the opponent's strategies and minimal approach to the subset can determine the optimal game outcome.

The fluctuation theorems provide an understanding of the relationship between two spectral densities in Gaussian processes, where single-trajectory spectral densities are analyzed for their relationship, and it's shown that a power law correlation function leads to a specific power law relationship, while a linear linear linear linear linear Gaussian process exhibits a linear correlation, and it's also shown that a single time-series can produce a power law relationship, and a comparison is made between the spectral densities of single and many-trajectory linear Gaussian processes.

This paper delves into the interaction between soliton and breather solutions of the one and one-dimensional Broer-Kaup system, employing the Backlund map and Lie algebra method. The system, initially presented in 1975 by N. Broer, exhibits a wide range of applications across various fields including ocean dynamics, nonlinear optics, and quantum theory, and is notable for its Lax pair and Hamiltonian structure. The work investigates the interaction of soliton and breather solutions via the B\"acklund transformation's connection relation, leading to the derivation of new solutions through the Lie algebra method. The paper also examines the application of this method to the one-dimensional Broer-Kaup system's generalised version, which was previously derived by the author.

This study demonstrates that in the presence of a certain condition in three-dimensional space, non-smooth solutions to a modified Euler equations set retain energy. To achieve this, we introduce a condition involving the large-scale behavior of the vorticity gradient, where the vorticity gradient's angular component is bounded by a certain variable-based function. The main proof relies on a novel approach to translate the preservation of energy into the convergence of a certain integral, where the proof of the convergence relies on a method combining compactness and algebraic cancellation.

We introduce VIRUP, a groundbreaking VR experience that reimagines virtual reality in innovative ways. Through VIRUP, users engage with a dynamic and interactive environment where they assume the role of an 'observer,' a term coined by John Wheeler in 1927. As an observer, users contribute to the evolution of an artificial universe, addressing fundamental questions about the nature of reality. By merging user input with cutting-edge AI techniques, VIRUP creates an ever-changing, immersive universe, offering a one-of-a-kind, time-limited experience. VIRUP's unique, dynamic universe is generated in real-time using a custom-built, universe-specific version of the popular game engine, Unity. The platform is designed to be user-friendly, with a straightforward interface and comprehensive guidelines. VIRUP is now available for testing and public feedback, with a special event scheduled at the CERN Compute Program's Industry Day on October 4, 2023.

The advent of big data and its applications in various fields has sparked interest in teaching data concepts to students in elementary school and middle school.

To address this need, we developed a data teaching system called Space Voyage, which utilizes physicalization to help students understand data. Our system consists of a data brick, a mechanical planet model, and a life-size map, allowing students to engage in hands-on data activities. These activities include learning about data types, practicing data analysis, and gaining an overview of geographical data.

Our evaluation of Space Voyage involved a controlled experiment with 93 students, aged 9-12, from three schools. Our results show that students using Space Voyage demonstrated significant improvements in their understanding of data, their ability to analyze data, and their knowledge of geographical information.

Identifying the flow of data in computer networks is a critical function that aids administrators in diagnosing and resolving issues. This data, known as a netflow, is a record of packets transmitted between a source and destination IP addresses. In a software-defined network, these data packets are aggregated and sent to a collector for analysis. The flow of data in these networks is a record of packets transmitted between specific IP addresses, and is a critical component in understanding network traffic. This paper presents a method for identifying these data flows in software-defined networks that leverages a database to minimize the amount of data sent to the collector for analysis. This approach enables a more efficient transfer of data from the data-plane to the controller, and is suitable for use in a variety of network configurations.

Recent advancements in VAEs have led to the development of several disentangled representation learning techniques. Although existing methods primarily utilize individual data instances, our approach leverages the relational information present in pairs of data instances. By incorporating relational relations into generative models using auto-encoders and VAEs, we achieve weak disentanglement. Our experiments demonstrate that utilizing relational information enhances the disentanglement of representations and results in more accurate reconstructions.

Researchers have developed oscillating foil systems that exploit the wake field to amplify energy recovery, achieving higher efficiency through various configurations. This study investigates the energy collection efficiency of tandem oscillating foils by analyzing the wake-foil interaction and energy transfer in both scenarios. A 2D Navier-Stokes solver, MIKE-2, was employed to model the dynamic behavior of the wake and foil surfaces in the Tandem-Wake-Sheet Configuration. The study examines the wake shape, surface velocity, and energy transfer within the tandem system and compares it with the single-foil system. Results show that the wake in the tandem system is more complex, with increased wake amplitude and velocity. However, the energy collection efficiency in the tandem system is comparable to that of the single-foil system.

We've developed a Bayesian method to estimate the real-time dynamics of lattice QCD by simulating the evolution of physical systems. Our approach allows for the precise calculation of real-time observables, like correlation functions, which are typically estimated based on their equilibrium values. However, the real-time dynamics of these observables often exhibit non-stationary patterns, necessitating a more nuanced understanding. Our Bayesian framework, drawing from the fields of machine learning and Bayesian inference, provides a novel solution to this challenge. We demonstrate the efficacy of this method by applying it to the real-time evolution of the gluon field within the Yang-Mills regime, using data from lattice QCD simulations. Our results reveal that the Bayesian method outperforms traditional estimation techniques in accurately capturing the real-time dynamics of these systems.

Quantum dots linked to superconducting islands through leads can exhibit charge tunneling, which may appear as charge-tunneling peaks or irregular conductance patterns in the quantum dot's resistance.  Despite the complexity of these phenomena, researchers have developed a new approach using gate sensing to distinguish between two possible mechanisms: Andreev and Cooper pair tunneling.  This distinction is made possible by analyzing the quantum dot's resistance while varying the gate voltage, and then correlating the resulting patterns with the Andreev and Cooper pair tunneling theories.  This dual analysis enables the identification of the dominant tunneling mechanism and allows for the determination of the tunneling amplitude and the superconducting energy gap.

The primary goal of the field of drug discovery is to identify novel molecules that effectively interact with a target protein. Recent advancements in generative models have enabled the creation of novel compounds by learning from existing collections of approved and rejected molecules. Despite these improvements, current models are often hindered by the limited availability of relevant data and the complexity of the chemical space in question. To address these challenges, we introduce an energy-driven generative model, which integrates the Protein-Ligand Score to predict the binding affinity of generated molecules with the target protein. Our model's performance was evaluated on a dataset of 12,997 molecules, and it successfully produced molecules with a binding affinity of up to -9.7 kcal/mol. Furthermore, we demonstrate the potential of our approach by applying it to the development of novel molecules for the COVID-19 pandemic using the ChEMBL database.

The Graph Token Guided Device (GTGD) is an interactive device that transforms
input programming tokens into a network of tokens and locations. Unlike static
devices like Graph Token Guided Reduction (GTGR), GTGD supports token movement,
creating dynamic graphs that mirror execution paths. By drawing inspiration from
the Geometry of Interaction (GOI) and leveraging a token-driven approach, GTGD
converts token graphs into directed graphs, effectively capturing sequential
computation processes. As tokens interact, the resulting graph evolves, tracing
program execution and reducing programs through dynamic graph reduction.

The Large Magellanic Cloud is a unique astronomical subject due to its intricate structure and complex interactions with its companion, the Small Magellanic Cloud. The clouds' interaction is thought to be mediated by the halo, which contains the majority of the system's mass. The spatial dynamics of the clouds are heavily influenced by the tidal forces exerted by the Milky Way, particularly the effect of its Gaia-like satellite, which is the Victoria-Tech telescope. The data collected by the VISTA survey in the Ks band allows for the creation of a detailed map of the LMC's outer regions, which is presented in this study. The study's findings reveal that the LMC is moving away from the SMC, with a significant 1.5 kiloparsec separation between the clouds. The data also suggests that the LMC is rotating in the direction opposite to the SMC, which is consistent with previous research. The study's analysis of the LMC's outer regions reveals that the clouds' interaction has a profound impact on their interaction. The data also provides insight into the LMC's rotation curve, which is consistent with a previously observed trend of decreasing rotation velocity with increasing distance from the LMC's center.

The increasing adoption of Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) systems has led to improved efficiency in meter reading and energy management. However, this system also exposes a vulnerability to Power Theft, allowing malicious manipulation of energy consumption data. To counteract this issue, this study introduces an advanced Power Theft detection system, leveraging Deep Recurrent Neural Networks (DNN) to analyze AMI data. The proposed system overcomes limitations in previous approaches, which relied on static data analysis. By incorporating real-time data, the model can detect Power Theft more effectively. To optimize the system's performance, we develop a new approach to adjust the Deep Recurrent neural network's hyper-parameters for improved results. This novel approach is validated through experiments using real-world data from a smart grid system, demonstrating its superiority over existing methods in detecting Power Theft accurately and reducing false positives.

For any compact surface $M$, there exists a sequence of surfaces $M_i$, each with negative genus, such that the sequence's sequence of surface graphs $G_i$ converges to the surface graph $G$ of $M$. The sequence's speed of convergence is proportional to the reciprocal of $i$'s cube. Additionally, for any compact surface $M$ with genus greater than zero, there exists a sequence of negative genus surfaces $M_i$ and their surface graphs $G_i$, such that as $i$ approaches infinity, the sequence of graphs $G_i$ converges to the surface graph $L(K_2)$ of the complete graph of length two.

The lifetime of the $\Omega^{0}_{c}$ baryon has been measured for the first time by analyzing data collected by the LHCb detector with a luminosity of 3 inverse femtobarns. This data was collected at proton-proton collisions occurring at 13 TeV. A precision of 60 millisecond has been achieved for the lifetime of the $\Omega^{0}_{c}$, while a preliminary lifetime of 14 millisecond has been reported for the $\Xi^{0}_{c}$ baryon. Both baryons were produced through the process $p\!+\!\bar{p}\!+\\to\Xi^{0}_{c}\!+\!\Xi^{0}_{c}\!+\!\pi^{-}\!+\!\pi^{+}\!+\!\pi^{-}\!+\!\pi^{+}$.

Hyperspectral images have become increasingly significant in remote sensing and have seen extensive use in classification tasks. However, the inherent characteristics of these images often lead to significant differences in local neighborhoods, posing a challenge to classification accuracy. To address this issue, the subspace clustering framework has been developed to identify homogeneous clusters within HSIs, thereby enhancing classification performance. However, the existing subspace clustering methods often suffer from a trade-off between speed and accuracy, necessitating a balance between efficiency and effectiveness. To address this challenge, a novel rapid and efficient clustering framework, named RASC, has been proposed to address this trade-off issue. The proposed framework consists of two key components, a similarity-constrained clustering method and a subspace projection algorithm, which are designed to be highly efficient and accurate. The similarity-constrained clustering method leverages the inherent similarity within local neighborhoods to identify homogeneous clusters, while the subspace projection algorithm further refines these clusters by projecting them onto a unified subspace. To optimize the efficiency of the framework, the proposed subspace projection algorithm utilizes a novel subspace search strategy to efficiently explore the subspace and select the most effective projection matrix. To evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed framework, a series of experiments were conducted on three real-world hyperspectral datasets, demonstrating its superiority over existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of both speed and accuracy.

The internal deformation of Arctic sea ice is a significant process that affects both the ice itself and the surrounding environment. Research has shown that deformed sea ice creates a complex snow topography due to the uneven distribution of snow load, which can lead to ice deformation. An idealized one-dimensional model has been developed to simulate the snow topography above deformed sea ice, taking into account the uneven distribution of snow cover and the effect of wind on snow accumulation. The model has been applied to a specific location and the results match observations from the Fram Strait. It was found that the snow topography is influenced by wind patterns and the distribution of snow cover, as well as the effect of katabatic winds on snow accumulation. The model has been applied to a different location and the results indicate that the snow topography is controlled by wind patterns and the effect of katabatic winds on snow accumulation. It is suggested that the model can be used to study the effect of sea ice deformation on snow topography in other regions, as long as the underlying wind patterns are similar.

We investigate the quantum Zeno effect in ultracold atom-molecule scattering within a periodic magnetic field. By applying pulsed magnetic fields, we demonstrate that the scattering can be completely prevented by synchronizing the magnetic field pulses with the resonant scattering frequency. Furthermore, we analyze the effect's dependence on the initial molecule phase and the time interval between the magnetic field pulses. Our results show that the quantum Zeno effect can be experimentally realized in a one-dimensional optical lattice, utilizing a combination of a periodic magnetic field and spatially uniform pulsed magnetic field resonating with the atom-molecule scattering frequency. The dynamic magnetic field effectively simulates the time-dependent Hamiltonian of the Bloch model, resulting in the Landau-Zener-Stueckelberg interference phenomenon.

We investigate the evolution of a system described by non-extensive It\^o-Stochastic
Langevin dynamics, which deviates from the standard exponential decay through
power-law correlations resulting from q-Gaussian distributions (where q is a
positive and quadratic index). A novel probability density function is introduced,
along with the associated q-Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution, to model the
non-equilibrium system. It is observed that the system's evolution can be accurately
represented by a q-Gaussian probability density, with the parameter evolving over
time according to a q-Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution, governed by a q-Maxwell-Boltzmann
equation. A q-Maxwell-Boltzmann equation is also derived for the q-Gaussian probability
density, which is analogous to the traditional Maxwell-Boltzmann equation for the
Gaussian probability density under standard dynamics. This research provides a framework
for the non-equilibrium modeling of q-Gaussian probability densities, with the
q-parameter acting as a control parameter.

A theoretical model is developed to describe optical excitation of a one-dimensional photonic crystal with modulated refractive index, resulting in a two-dimensional system with non-Hermitian nodal lines. This system hosts Weyl points with complex momentum space properties, featuring a twist in complex momentum space. The system's topological properties are characterized by domain wall states with non-Hermitian interface topological numbers, which are observed in numerical simulations of time-domain optical pulse propagation experiments. The system's unique higher-order topological properties are confirmed by detecting domain wall states with a nodal line as their boundary.

The rise of blockchain technology has led to a surge in research into distributed computing systems. However, existing blockchain-based distributed computing protocols often struggle with two key issues: they are either inherently incompatible with traditional virtual machines, or they lack a reward mechanism to incentivize participation. This paper presents Marvel DC, a distributed computing protocol that addresses these limitations by integrating a Delegated Proportional Consensus module with the Framework of Virtual Machine. Furthermore, we propose a reward distribution plan that motivates nodes to participate in distributed computing.

This research proposes a reduced reference quality assessment framework tailored to 3D point cloud compression, which is more efficient than full reference methods. The framework incorporates two metrics, including a distortion-based metric and a separate metric quantifying the difference in quality. The framework's application in rate-distortion point cloud compression is demonstrated, and its performance is evaluated through a series of experiments.

In holographic QCD, we explore the thermal phase transition and single-critical-point diagram in the quark-mass deformation region, finding that the phase transition can be non-singular and is influenced by the quark mass. We establish that the deconfinement-complementarity phase transition is a separate occurrence from the chiral symmetry-breaking phase transition, and that non-Abelian gauge fields play a pivotal role in this phenomenon.

The use of deep learning for identifying anomalies in medical images has gained significant attention, yet most existing methods solely rely on self-supervised learning and overlook the importance of pre-processing these complex, multi-modal data. We introduce a novel slice-based self-supervised learning framework, specifically designed for evaluating knee health using MRI scans, which is crucial for diagnosing conditions such as osteoarthritis. Our approach involves a multi-modal preprocessing step that extracts meaningful features from MRI data and integrates them into a transformer network for anomaly detection. We compare the performance of our framework with traditional supervised learning and existing state-of-the-art anomaly detection methods, achieving superior results in all cases.

The objective of typeface design is to create a distinctive visual style for written text. Although numerous typefaces have been developed, there is still a need for more. This research presents a new method for rapidly generating typefaces by learning the styles of a small collection of existing typefaces. Given a collection of typefaces and a text sample, the goal is to produce a new typeface that captures the style of the collection while preserving the original text layout. Our method involves analyzing the local features of characters and text tokens to identify style components. We employ a transformer-based model to learn the complex relationships between characters and use a convolutional model to capture the styles of local character components. By combining these learned representations, we can generate the style of the collection for any text. Our experiments demonstrate that our typeface generation method produces high-quality, visually consistent typefaces that capture the style of the training examples.

We introduce a novel class of anomalous fluids characterized by their unusual, nonhomogeneous spatial structure, which arises from the interplay between thermal fluctuations and the presence of chiral, two-dimensional torsions. We demonstrate that these fluids can be described by a specific model incorporating temperature and chirality-dependent terms, which captures the distinctive, nonstandard properties exhibited by these fluids. Furthermore, we explore the implications of these models for the behavior of thermodynamic properties such as the free energy, which can be mathematically represented by a refined version of the Landau theory, taking into account the chiral torsional influences.

This study introduces an advanced approach for enhancing the quality of experience (QoE) in adaptive video streaming through a digital twin-based framework. The proposed system utilizes personalized QoE metrics, including mean opinion score (MOS) and buffer dynamics, to optimize video content delivery. The system's architecture consists of a digital twin platform, where a cloud-based controller and local controllers work in tandem to improve QoE. The cloud controller utilizes a deep learning model to predict user-specific MOS and buffer dynamics, while the local controller dynamically adjusts video content delivery at edge nodes based on real-time network conditions and predicted QoE metrics. The effectiveness of this approach is demonstrated through experiments using real-world video content and network environments.

In the context of the KM3NeT detector, a novel approach for reconstructing double-waterfalls in neutrino fluxes has been developed. This method is now being implemented within the detector's analysis chain and its performance is being evaluated using actual detector data.

We're focusing on the periodic nonlinear Schrödinger equation with a specific type of noise added to its function. The term causing the disturbance has a specific pattern, and its influence decreases as it moves further away. Building on earlier work that proved the equation is stable under certain conditions, we're taking it a step further by examining how well the system behaves when looking at a very small scale. The main goal here is to understand how this system behaves when looking at its individual parts, a challenge that has been a hard one, but we've been able to make some progress.

Ensuring timely and reliable data transmission in machine-type communication is a complex task due to the numerous devices that need to be supported, the limited resources available, and the varying wireless channel conditions. To address these challenges, we propose a new approach that simultaneously allocates resources to each device and encodes the data transmitted over multiple, parallel wireless channels. Our method is designed to achieve a balance between energy efficiency and meeting the required latency constraints for different reliability levels. To simplify the resource allocation process, we first transform the joint allocation and encoding problem into a new format, and then develop an efficient algorithm that solves it quickly. Our proposed solution outperforms existing methods in terms of energy efficiency, particularly in situations with poor wireless channel conditions, while meeting the set latency and reliability targets.

The Sgr A East supernova remnant, located near the center of the Milky Way, poses a significant challenge to researchers. Its proximity to the Galactic center raises questions about the supernova's origin, with some speculating it may have been triggered by the galaxy's gravitational field. To address these doubts, we conducted a simulation to determine if the supernova remnant resulted from a supernova explosion occurring at varying distances from the Galactic center. The findings indicate that the supernova likely originated at least 30 parsecs from the Galactic center and took approximately 20 to 30 thousand years to travel towards the current location of Sgr A East, with an acceleration of 100 to 200 km/s/kyr. These results are consistent with the properties of Type Ia supernovae and suggest that the supernova likely originated from an old, low-mass, single-star system.

A fundamental principle in the Standard Model, lepton flavor universality, has been observed to be disrupted in certain B-meson decay processes that involve third-generation leptons. This discrepancy is observed in two main areas:  \textit{(i)} a significant deviation from the lepton flavor universality ratio in certain B decays, which involves b to s lepton processes, as recorded by LHCb;  \textit{(ii)} a significant deviation from the lepton flavor universality ratio in certain B decays, which involves b to c processes, as recorded by LHCb. This discrepancy is found to be statistically significant. Both findings are in line with current theoretical models within their respective uncertainties. This discussion will cover the current state of measurements, the associated uncertainties, and possible theoretical explanations.

This research paper outlines our system's approach to the 2021 DISRPT shared task, focusing on discourse segmentation, categorization, and connection identification in written text. We developed a unified architecture that leverages a combination of pre-trained features and in-scope representations, incorporating both automated and human-annotated inferences. We employed a multi-task learning framework to enhance the performance of our downstream models, as well as integrated a variety of inference methods to improve the accuracy of our connection detection model. Our proposed system achieved notable results, ranking first in connection detection and second in discourse segmentation, outperforming the other competing approaches.

The advent of 6G and beyond wireless communication technology is poised to revolutionize the way various vertical industries interact with underlying wireless-infrastructure. To address the numerous challenges that arise in sharing infrastructure among these diverse sectors, a groundbreaking solution has been developed. This solution, known as Blockchain-Enabled Accountable and Clear Infrastructure Sharing (BEACONS), is a cutting-edge framework that leverages blockchain technology to ensure seamless and secure infrastructure sharing. To tackle the complexities of multiple Vertical-Vertical-Infrastructure (VVI) interactions, BEACONS employs a sophisticated multi-agent system comprising multiple blockchain-based entities. These entities, including the Infrastructure Owner, Infrastructure-as-a-Service Provider, and Infrastructure Consumer, are facilitated by the BEACONS Intelligent Agent, which enables effortless infrastructure sharing. To ensure the security of these blockchain-based entities, the solution incorporates advanced security features, such as a multi-layered architecture and a robust consensus algorithm. To validate the effectiveness of BEACONS, a comprehensive simulation study was conducted, which demonstrated the solution's ability to ensure clear and accountable infrastructure sharing. To the knowledge of the authors, BEACONS is the pioneering infrastructure-sharing framework that leverages blockchain technology to tackle the numerous challenges associated with VVI interactions.

This article provides an in-depth examination of the Okubo-Weiss criterion, a fundamental concept in understanding the dynamics of 2D fluids and plasmas. The criterion is directly related to the conditions under which linearized 2D hydrodynamics and magnetohydrodynamics exhibit elliptical flow characteristics. The study derives the Okubo-Weiss criteria for both barotropic and baroclinic fluids, as well as 2D magnetohydrodynamics, and presents a simplified representation of these conditions. The findings are further supported by numerical simulations of the MHD version of the quasi-2D Kelvin-Helmholtz instability, which demonstrate the emergence of elliptical structures in the presence of strong magnetic fields.

This paper explores the thermal behavior of a Lee-Wick field theory at low temperatures, discovering that it exhibits characteristics of a condensate. We found that the early universe's effective Hamiltonian, incorporating Lee-Wick fields, shares similarities with a free field theory, albeit with a different renormalization procedure and cosmological constant. Consequently, the presence of Lee-Wick fields does not give rise to the big bang singularity, and their effect on the early universe's expansion is comparable to that of a free field.

The goal of image style transfer is to create a novel image that effectively combines the contents of two separate images, specifically their respective styles. In this research, we introduce a new approach to image style transfer using a transformer-based framework that incorporates a style embedding block and a style residual block. Our method employs the Vision Transformer as its foundation, leveraging its ability to process images in a holistic manner and analyze long-range dependencies. Our approach uses the style embedding block to encode the style information of two images, while the style residual block uses multi-head attention to fuse the encoded styles into the image. Our method can be trained in a self-supervised manner using a single loss function. Our experiments demonstrate that our method can achieve state-of-the-art results in both image style translation and image style transfer tasks. Our method can also be trained in a more efficient manner. Our method's code will be made publicly available.

The minimum amount of heat that needs to be produced during the erasure process can be calculated using the minimum work required to erase a specified amount of information, and this is in accordance with Landauer's principle.
